narrative.overview:
A clean roster on a cool desk on the morning of Service Day: names, places, deadlines, all in ink, and one green mark beside whatever is filling up. Service Day sits on a cool, faintly green-grey canvas with white cards laid on it like sheets: large soft corners, almost no lines, no shadows at rest. Ink does the acting: the primary button, the page you are on, the filter you chose. Pine does the counting: slot meters, chart bars, the participation gauge. Everything else is ink on white.

This is a working dashboard (Operate). Ambition shows as precision and restraint: confident numbers set large in tabular figures, medium-weight headings, small muted labels, and generous but never empty spacing. Pill-shaped controls and thin line icons keep the surface soft without making it cute. Typography follows `docs/reference/dashboard-reference.png`; the colour mood (ink selection, pale cool canvas, muted pastels for categories) was chosen with the student from a second reference, without its decorative backdrop.

The scene that sets the theme: office staff at a desk in daylight, and on the day itself a phone outdoors, so the default is light. Every value here is the light theme; a dark theme is not part of this build.
keyCharacteristics: Cool light canvas, white cards, flat at rest; depth only on overlays.
Ink for action and selection; pine for marks that count. Neither is used as decoration.
Large tabular numerals for anything counted: slots, participation, days left.
Status is shown with the same small vocabulary everywhere (open, last slots, closing soon, full, closed, cancelled, draft), always with a label.

Signature details carry the identity: the segmented **slot meter**, the relative + absolute **cut-off label**, the bar-built **participation gauge**, and **initials avatars** on deterministic muted tints for NGOs.

rules.name: The One Dark Item Rule
rules.body: In any group (navigation, filters, tabs, a card's actions) at most one element is filled with Ink: the current or primary one. Hover never fills with Ink; it uses Hairline or Sunken Paper, so the current item stays unmistakable.

rules.name: The Pine Counts Rule
rules.body: Pine appears on marks that measure something (places, participation, fill), never as a fill behind content areas or as decoration. Success keeps its own leaf-green hue so "open" never reads as "pine".

rules.name: The Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every text/background pair in this palette is at least 4.5:1 and every control edge at least 3:1; keep it that way when adding tokens.

rules.name: The No Hard-Coding Rule
rules.body: Component CSS uses these tokens through CSS custom properties in `src/styles/tokens.css`; no hex values, font sizes or radii in component files. Canvas-drawn things (the Fill by NGO chart, the QR code and its PNG poster) read the same tokens with `getComputedStyle`.

rules.name: The Field Edge Rule
rules.body: Anything you type into gets the `control-border` edge. Buttons and pills don't: their label identifies them, so they keep the quiet `hairline-strong` outline or none.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Sentence case everywhere: headings, buttons, labels, pills. No all-caps labels, no tracked-out eyebrows.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or be compared uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so live counts don't jitter.

rules.name: The Three Weights Rule
rules.body: Only 400, 500 and 600. Headings are 500; 600 is reserved for rare emphasis inside text.

rules.name: The Stacked Row Rule
rules.body: A table never makes the page scroll sideways. When it doesn't fit, its rows become stacked blocks; the data stays, the columns go.

rules.name: The Flat Table Rule
rules.body: Cards never get borders or shadows at rest. If a card needs separation, adjust the surface tone, not a line.

dos: keep Ink for action and selection, Pine for marks that count, and use `accent-strong` for any pine-coloured text.
give every data view a loading skeleton, an empty state that says what to do next, and an error state.
explain every disabled action in a sentence ("Registration closed on 18 Nov, 17:00").
show deadlines relative and absolute together: "Closes in 2 days · 18 Nov, 17:00".
let card sizes follow their content and importance; a KPI row and a chart card are not the same weight.
keep a visible `:focus-visible` ring on every interactive element.
give text fields the Field Edge (`control-border`) and keep every interactive target at least 24px.
put the number in tabular figures and the meaning in a muted label next to it ("50 of 64 staff have a place").
donts: use decorative gradients, glassmorphism or blur panels, or purple-blue palettes.
use emoji as icons, heavy drop shadows, or decorative illustrations that carry no information.
fill screens with identical cards in a uniform grid, or center everything.
use all-caps headings or put an icon on every heading.
use lorem ipsum or placeholder names ("Activity 1", "John Doe"); seed content is specific and fictional.
reproduce the look of a Bootstrap admin template or Material defaults.
cut names, titles or places off with an ellipsis; let them wrap.
line up a column of red "Delete" buttons; destructive actions go in the row's ⋯ menu and through a confirm dialog.
